content: Abraham et al. (1998) evaluated two immunochromatographic assays for their effectiveness in rapid screening of hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) in the Indian Journal of Medical Microbiology. Similarly, Akanmu et al. (2006) assessed a rapid test kit for detecting HBsAg and HBeAg in whole blood, proposing its potential use for pre-donation testing in the African Journal of Medicine and Medical Sciences. Bottero et al. (2013) analyzed the performance of rapid tests for detecting HBsAg and anti-HBs antibodies in a large cohort in France, as reported in the Journal of Hepatology. Chameera et al. (2013) examined the diagnostic efficacy of rapid assays for detecting hepatitis B virus surface antigen in Sri Lanka, published in the Sri Lankan Journal of Infectious Diseases. Clement et al. (2002) evaluated a new rapid test for the combined detection of HBsAg and HBeAg in the Journal of Clinical Microbiology. Davies et al. (2010) investigated the reliability of rapid testing for hepatitis B in regions with high HIV prevalence, as detailed in the Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene. Franzcek et al. (2013) explored the use of rapid diagnostic tests for HBsAg screening among HIV-infected patients in rural Tanzania, published in PLoS One. Kaur et al. (2000) assessed rapid kits for detecting HIV, HBsAg, and HCV infections in the Indian Journal of Medical Sciences. Khan et al. (2010) compared the performance of two rapid immunochromatographic tests for detecting HBsAg and anti-HCV antibodies using ELISA-tested samples, as reported in AKEMU. Lau et al. (2003) described a rapid immunochromatographic assay for hepatitis B virus screening in the Journal of Viral Hepatitis. Lien et al. (2000) evaluated rapid diagnostic tests for detecting HIV types 1 and 2, HBsAg, and syphilis in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, as published in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene. Another study in 2008 assessed a new HBsAg rapid test with improved sensitivity in the Journal of Clinical Microbiology. Mvere et al. (1996) reported encouraging results from simple hepatitis assays in a blood donor population in Zimbabwe, published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization. Oh et al. (1999) evaluated the Genedia® HBsAg Rapid and Genedia® anti-HBs Rapid tests for HBsAg and anti-HBs screening in the Korean Journal of Clinical Pathology. Ola et al. (2009) highlighted diagnostic challenges in hepatitis B virus infection among Nigerian adults in the Nigerian Journal of Clinical Practice. Raj et al. (2001) assessed an indigenously manufactured rapid immunochromatographic test for HBsAg detection in the Indian Journal of Pathology and Microbiology. Randrianirina et al. (2008) evaluated the performance of four rapid tests for HBsAg detection in Madagascar, as reported in the Journal of Virological Methods. Sato et al. (1996) assessed immunochromatographic assay systems for rapid detection of HBsAg and antibodies in the Journal of Clinical Microbiology. Bjorkvoll et al. (2010) examined the accuracy of screening tests for HBsAg, anti-HBc, and anti-HCV among potential blood donors in rural Cambodia and Vietnam, published in the Southeast Asian Journal of Tropical Medicine and Public Health. Chevaliez et al. (2014) evaluated a new rapid test for HBsAg detection across various patient populations in the Journal of Clinical Virology. Erhabor et al. (2013) compared ELISA and rapid screening techniques for HBsAg detection among blood donors in Nigeria, as reported in the Journal of Blood and Lymph. Gish et al. (2014) described a simple and cost-effective point-of-care test for HBsAg detection in the Journal of Viral Hepatitis. Geretti et al. (2010) identified a high prevalence of hepatitis B virus co-infection among HIV-positive individuals in Ghana, as published in the Journal of Clinical Microbiology. Hoffmann et al. (2012) explored the prevalence and associations of hepatitis B and C infections among HIV-infected adults in South Africa, reported in the International Journal of STD & AIDS. Hønge et al. (2014) noted that rapid tests for HBsAg and anti-HCV underestimated hepatitis prevalence among HIV-infected patients, as detailed in HIV Medicine. Mutocheluh et al. Njai et al. (2015) validated rapid point-of-care tests for HBsAg detection in field and laboratory settings in The Gambia, as reported in the Journal of Clinical Microbiology. Nyirenda et al. (2008) examined the prevalence of hepatitis B and C infections and co-infection with HIV among medical inpatients in Malawi, published in the Journal of Infection. Upreti et al. (2014) assessed the prevalence of chronic hepatitis B virus infection before and after implementing a vaccination program among children in Nepal, as reported in Vaccine. Liu et al. (2014) evaluated four methods for HBsAg detection and their application in testing over 116,000 specimens, published in the Journal of Virological Methods. Ol et al. (2009) reported on the prevalence of hepatitis B and C infections among potential blood donors in rural Cambodia, as detailed in the Southeast Asian Journal of Tropical Medicine and Public Health. Peng et al. (2011) developed an economic and efficient strategy for HBsAg detection using gray zones in ELISA and combined detection assays, published in Clinica Chimica Acta. Viet et al. (2012) examined the prevalence of hepatitis B and C infections among potential blood donors in rural Vietnam, as reported in the Indian Journal of Medical Research. Ansari et al. (2007) compared rapid diagnostic tests and PCR methods for HBsAg detection in Iran, published in Hepatitis Monthly. Nakata and Johnson (1990) evaluated a rapid immunoconcentration assay for HBsAg detection in a prison inmate population, presented at the American Society for Microbiology Annual Meeting. Palmer et al. (1999) conducted a multicenter evaluation of Determine™ rapid tests for diagnosing HIV, HBsAg, and syphilis, presented at the Interscience Conference on Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy. Torane and Shastri (2008) compared ELISA and rapid screening tests for diagnosing HIV, hepatitis B, and hepatitis C among healthy blood donors in Mumbai, published in the Indian Journal of Medical Microbiology. Cha et al. (2006) evaluated indigenously manufactured immunochromatographic assay systems for rapid HBsAg and antibody detection, published in the Korean Journal of Laboratory Medicine. Whang and Um (2005) compared immunochromatography assays and quantitative immunoassays for detecting HBsAg and anti-HBs, as reported in the Korean Journal of Laboratory Medicine. Maity et al. (2012) assessed the performance of ELISA and rapid kits for detecting HIV, HBV, and HCV in India, published in Virology Journal. Lukhwareni et al. (2009) reported increased detection of HBV DNA in HBsAg-positive and HBsAg-negative South African HIV/AIDS patients enrolling for antiretroviral therapy, published in the Journal of Medical Virology. Mphahlele et al. (2006) highlighted the high risk of occult hepatitis B infection in HIV-positive patients in South Africa, as reported in the Journal of Clinical Virology. Khadem-Ansari et al. (2014) compared chemiluminescent and PCR methods for HBV detection in clinical laboratories, published in Advanced Biomedical Research. Nna et al. (2014) reported occult hepatitis B infection among blood donors in southeastern Nigeria, published in Pathogens and Global Health. Olinger et al. (2007) evaluated the diagnostic impact of mutations in the preS/S gene on HBsAg detection in Nigeria, published in Medical Microbiology and Immunology. Seremba et al. (2010) validated the rapid strip assay test for HBsAg detection in hospitalized patients in Uganda, published in the Journal of Medical Virology. Shivkumar et al. (2012) conducted a meta-analysis of rapid point-of-care tests for hepatitis B infection, published in the American Journal of Gastroenterology. Mudawi et al. (2014) examined overt and occult HBV infection in Sudanese HIV patients, published in the International Journal of Infectious Diseases. N'Dri-Yoman et al. (2010) reported occult HBV infection in untreated HIV-infected adults in Côte d'Ivoire, published in Antiviral Therapy. Laperche et al. (2013) assessed blood-borne virus testing and transfusion safety across Africa, published in Transfusion. Pruett et al. (2015) reviewed the use of rapid diagnostic tests for transfusion infectious screening in Africa, published in Transfusion Medicine Reviews. Scheiblauer et al. (2010) evaluated 70 HBsAg assays globally, considering HBV genotypes and HBsAg subtypes, published in Vox Sanguinis. Another study in 2006 evaluated 17 CE-marked HBsAg assays for clinical sensitivity and mutant detection, published in the Journal of Medical Virology. Mizuochi et al. (2006) evaluated 10 commercial diagnostic kits for in vitro expressed HBsAgs encoded by HBV genotypes A to H, published in the Journal of Virological Methods. Ly et al. (2006) assessed the sensitivity of four commercial HBsAg assays for detecting mutant forms, published in the Journal of Clinical Microbiology. Moerman et al. (2004) evaluated the sensitivity of four HBsAg assays for wild-type and mutant forms, published in Clinical Laboratory. Zhang et al. (2010) examined HBV transfusion risk in China, published in Transfusion Medicine. Martin et al. (2012) correlated improved HBsAg detection limits with HBV DNA nucleic acid test yield in blood donations, published in Transfusion. Austin (2005) compared the sensitivity and specificity of two rapid HBsAg detection methods with a third-generation enzyme immunoassay, published in the New Zealand Journal of Medical Laboratory Science. Kuhns et al. (2007) reported the frequency of diagnostically significant HBsAg mutants, published in the Journal of Medical Virology. Servant-Delmas et al. (2012) evaluated the capacity of 13 HBsAg assays to detect mutants in blood samples, published in the Journal of Clinical Virology. Hirzel et al. (2015) assessed the performance of HBsAg point-of-care tests for detecting diagnostic escape variants, published in the Journal of Clinical Virology. Maylin et al. (2015) reported short-term spontaneous fluctuations of HBV DNA levels in a Senegalese population with chronic hepatitis B, published in BMC Infectious Diseases.
